mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate investments, which in turn negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over three consecutive months indicates a strengthening economy, boosting consumer confidence and spending, which positively affects S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 55% of the instances where HOUST increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3pp in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates increased economic activity, which positively impacts corporate earnings and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over three months, it indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and positively affects S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > CPIAUCSL growth over 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 55% of the instances where RSAFS growth exceeded CPIAUCSL growth over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase & UNRATE decrease in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased and UNRATE decreased in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: low interest rate with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was below 1% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month, coupled with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points, signals a weakening economy, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decrease > 1% & UNRATE increase > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 55% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% and UNRATE increased by more than 0.3pp in a month.
